items.title: Longineu Parsons interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 17, 2026
items.q: I came up in Cab Calloway’s band and playing shows and stuff, Broadway shows.

ctx.x: Yeah I think these lines that are placed between this and between that and all these things, these are artificial lines that people have placed. And that’s symbolic of the lines that we human beings place between each other in life, all over the world in all kinds of ways we have all of these lines that say I’m different from you. And that’s the biggest bunch of bullshit going in the world. You know this is what’s keeping us at war. This is what’s keeping us with all of this strife is that we make these lines…

a while. I get to know people who live in places. And people are people when it comes down to it. And then we’re saying, “Oh yeah but I don’t like them because they’re like this and –” it’s crazy. I know of people in Paris where you have Iranian and Israeli making music together. Now this is an example of how we humans need to learn how to live. My production company is Tribal Disorder Productions. We’re a force against the disorder in the human tribe. I know humanity is a species, not a tribe, but I’m using…

You made it your business to know where the exits were, right? I love your description. It reminds me of fellas like Joe Wilder and the long trek through all these different kinds of gigs and developing a work ethic which is so important, and making yourself stand out so your phone rings.
